action_summary: Rounds 23/24 measured compress-admit-license-replay for ONE family and pinned that generalisation was unshown. This round generalises the lifter itself -- every constant-collection literal (tuple/list/set/dict, recursively) lifts as ONE parameter, with None/True/False excluded as structural singletons (lifting them measured out as self-defeating: the abstraction grew a parameter every site passed as the same singleton, and the schema dict shredded) -- and fixes the helper renderer to indent every line of multi-line statements (the old renderer produced a SyntaxError on `if row is None:` bodies, swallowed and reported as no-shape, hidden since round 23 by single-line corpora). Prediction written before measurement: three world-model organs compress into one admitted abstraction with measured gain and the family recognised from structure; a never-seen fourth, built cold, replays strictly smaller with behaviour preserved. MEASURED: 2 sites NOT_COMPRESSIVE; 3 sites gain 103 bytes family keyed_table_lookup; never-seen organ 394 -> 277 bytes (30% smaller); 0 behaviour mismatches on held-out ids including unknowns and non-strings. Honesty upgrades the family forced, both pinned: a probe grid the original answers identically verifies nothing -- non-discriminating grids now refuse BOTH admission and replay (PROBE_GRID_NON_DISCRIMINATING); the bridge stays SKILL-only and admits nothing it cannot probe. The crystallization-time-emission candidate was killed with arithmetic before implementation: embedded-helper organs measure ~262 vs 179 bytes; emission only pays with a runtime-binding execution contract, an architectural decision out of round scope.
